entries.description: Chose the premise audit over the depth-3 session, on the reasoning that a fallen premise rots quietly and the audit is bounded and cheap while depth 3 is neither urgent nor at risk.

Enumerated the six NOT-AFFECTED documents rather than reporting only the three hits, so documents-examined equals documents-reported-on. A hit list alone lets the reader assume the search was exhaustive without evidence of its denominator.

Refused to report route 2 as refuted outright. mulTree carries two real hypotheses (1 < a.eval x, 0 < b.eval x); the corpus argument's REASONING is dead but its CONCLUSION may survive if its trees meet those bounds. Wrote the hypotheses into the theorem statement and recorded that nobody has checked.

findings.description: THREE corpus claims fell with the no-native-addition premise: the Lambert-W any-depth barrier's proposed route (its key sub-question answered YES by selfPlusLog_eval), the products/quotients reasoning in the differentiation-closure argument, and two entries in the 2026-06-13 overnight handoff. No shipped theorem was invalidated — every affected item is a route, conjecture, or cost estimate.
